hadith:
Virtues of the Qur'an - Narrated Sahl bin Sa`d:

A lady came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and declared that she had decided to offer herself to Allah and His Apostle. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I am not in need of women." A man said (to the Prophet) "Please marry her to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to him), "Give her a garment." The man said, "I cannot afford it." The Prophet said, "Give her anything, even if it were an iron ring." The man apologized again. The Prophet then asked him, "What do you know by heart of the Qur'an?" He replied, "I know such-andsuch portion of the Qur'an (by heart)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Then I marry her to you for that much of the Qur'an which you know by heart."
message: The warning in Qur’an 43:77–78 invites us to welcome the truth rather than resent it. Remembering Allah as Ar-Razzāq can strengthen our trust in His provision, while the hadith reminds us of the value of what we learn from the Qur’an.
name:
Ar Razzaaq - الرَّزَّاقُ - The Provider

Ar Razzaaq describes Allah as the giver of provision. Quran 51:58 joins this name with strength, showing that His giving does not arise from need or weakness. Provision includes nourishment and other gifts on which His creatures depend.
verse:
Az-Zukhruf - The Ornaments of Gold - 43:77-78

They will cry, “O Mâlik! Let your Lord finish us off.” He will answer, “You are definitely here to stay.”

We certainly brought the truth to you, but most of you were resentful of the truth.
